newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGEMENT HAVE CHANGE OF HEART.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS MANAGEMENT HAVE CHANGE OF HEART.

text.p: The British Lions' management have had a change of heart and will now announce their team in advance of the first test against South Africa at Newlands on Saturday.
Manager Fran Cotton said on Wednesday that the starting 15 and six replacements would be announced at 1300 South African time on Thursday.
Previously the Lions said they intended to keep their opponents guessing by delaying naming the side until shortly before kick-off.
"We thought it would be better to settle things down and let everyone focus on the test rather than have the press running round asking people if they were in or out," said coach Ian McGeechan.
"This way we can concentrate on the match."
The players were told of their fate on Wednesday morning when notes were posted under the each player's bedroom door at 7.45 a.m. by a Lions administrative assistant.
"We decided to do it this way before we even left the British Isles," said manager Fran Cotton.
"We discussed it with the players and we thought it would be better to give each individual a quiet hour to gather his thoughts before meeting up with the rest of the team.
"It's better this way than sitting all 35 down and saying 'you're in' or 'you're out'."
McGeechan said it had been the toughest selection meeting in his career -- lasting two hours.
"At this stage of the tour that's a pretty lengthy meeting. It didn't take that long to select the tour squad," added Cotton.
He said the side would be announced after they had had the chance to see how "one or two bumps and bruises" had settled down.
The three test series -- with tests in Durban and Johannesburg on the following two Saturdays -- is the first between the Lions and South Africa for 17 years.
